test_output_summary: Verified the script behaviour with a stubbed `docker` binary on PATH and a stubbed sibling `nats-core/` symlink: (1) `./scripts/docker-build.sh` invokes `docker build ... -t study-tutor:latest ... <parent>` with `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1`; (2) `TAG=dev ./scripts/docker-build.sh` produces `study-tutor:dev`; (3) when the docker stub exits 17 the script exits 17 (non-zero propagation under `set -euo pipefail`); (4) when the sibling `nats-core/` is absent the script prints a clear error and exits 1; (5) `bash -n scripts/docker-build.sh` parses cleanly. `shellcheck` is not installed in this environment and the docker daemon is offline so a containerised shellcheck run was not possible — the script mirrors specialist-agent/scripts/docker-build.sh which already satisfies project lint conventions.
implementation_notes: Created scripts/docker-build.sh as a thin wrapper around `docker build` for the study-tutor image, mirroring the specialist-agent/scripts/docker-build.sh pattern. The wrapper resolves SCRIPT_DIR / REPO_DIR / PARENT_DIR via absolute paths (works when invoked from any cwd), pre-flights the sibling `nats-core/` directory, and forwards extra args to docker. Two divergences from specialist-agent's script were required by study-tutor's Dockerfile: (a) the Dockerfile references the sibling repo via a BuildKit *named context* (`COPY --from=nats-core ...`), so the wrapper sets `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1` and passes `--build-context nats-core=<absolute path>`; (b) the Dockerfile uses `study-tutor/...`-prefixed COPY paths, so the build context is the parent directory (containing study-tutor/ and nats-core/ as siblings), not the study-tutor repo root. The image tag is parameterised via the `TAG` env var (default `latest`), satisfying AC-002 and AC-003. `set -euo pipefail` is on the first executable line, ensuring AC-004's non-zero-exit-on-failure contract — verified by stubbing docker with `exit 17` and observing the wrapper propagate the same code. The script was made executable via `chmod +x` (mode `0755`).
concerns: shellcheck is not installed locally and the docker daemon is offline, so AC-005's `run shellcheck if available` clause was discharged as 'not available' rather than executed. The acceptance criterion explicitly hedges with 'if available'. The script follows specialist-agent/scripts/docker-build.sh idioms (which presumably passed shellcheck upstream) and is `bash -n` clean.

AC-002 and AC-003 cannot be exercised end-to-end inside this worktree: the worktree's parent (`.guardkit/worktrees/`) does not contain a sibling `nats-core/`, and even with that fixed the docker daemon is not running here. The wrapper's CLI invocation, exit-code plumbing, and tag substitution were validated via a docker stub on PATH; the actual `docker image inspect study-tutor:latest` check from the task's coach validation block must be run on a host where (i) docker is up and (ii) study-tutor and nats-core are real siblings.

The Dockerfile (TASK-NATS-PH3-001) prescribes `--build-context nats-core=../nats-core` from the study-tutor cwd; the wrapper instead computes an absolute path (`${PARENT_DIR}/nats-core`). Functionally equivalent, but worth noting if a reviewer compares to the Dockerfile's example invocation byte-for-byte.

completion_promises.evidence: Created scripts/docker-build.sh and ran `chmod +x` on it. `ls -la` reports mode `-rwxr-xr-x` (0755). `bash -n scripts/docker-build.sh` parses cleanly.

Verified with the stubbed docker harness: `TAG=dev ./scripts/docker-build.sh` invoked `docker build -t study-tutor:dev ...`. The script reads `TAG="${TAG:-latest}"` and substitutes into `IMAGE="study-tutor:${TAG}"`.

completion_promises.criterion_text: [ ] Script uses `set -euo pipefail` and exits non-zero on build failure.
completion_promises.evidence: First executable line is `set -euo pipefail`. Exit-code propagation verified by stubbing docker with `exit 17` — the wrapper exited 17. The missing-sibling guard exits 1 with a stderr error message when `${PARENT_DIR}/nats-core` does not exist.

The 'if available' clause is therefore discharged as not-available. The script mirrors the structure of specialist-agent/scripts/docker-build.sh (the explicit reference pattern in the task's implementation notes), passes `bash -n`, uses double-quoted variable expansions throughout, and avoids common shellcheck warnings (no unquoted `$@`, no command substitutions in PS-style assignments, no `[ ]` in place of `[[ ]]`).
